tips: Never use crushed walnut shell (or other crushed nut shells) in a facial scrub — the shells fracture into jagged, serrated-edged shards that can cause micro-tears in skin. For the face choose round, smooth particles instead: spherical jojoba beads or fine sugar, which have rounded edges and dissolve or deform under pressure.

Emulsified scrubs (made with emulsifying wax) turn into a lotion-like layer and rinse clean with water; plain oil-and-sugar scrubs leave an oil film behind. Either way, always warn users that oil-based scrubs make the tub or shower floor dangerously slippery both during use and until the residue is cleaned off.

Any scrub used in the shower or dipped into with wet hands will get water in the jar, so it needs a broad-spectrum preservative: liquid Germall Plus at 0.1-0.5% (0.5% is the standard choice for scrubs) or Optiphen at 0.75-1.5% of total weight. Note Optiphen Plus is water-soluble and hard to incorporate into anhydrous scrubs — for purely oil-based formulas an oil-soluble preservative like Phenonip is the better fit.

Scrubs containing fresh, non-dehydrated ingredients (citrus peel or zest, fresh herbs, used coffee grounds) last only about 1-2 weeks even refrigerated — make small batches and store them in the fridge. By contrast, a plain sugar- or salt-plus-oil scrub keeps for months at room temperature and longer refrigerated, provided no water or wet fingers contaminate the jar.
